references.text: Esau lived in the Seir region, also known as Edom, which traces back to his settlement there.
After meeting Jacob, Esau returned to Seir, another name for Edom.
God reminds the Israelites not to disturb the Edomites because He has given the land of Seir to Esau as an inheritance.
Just as God gave the land of Seir to Esau and his descendants, a parallel to how He gave land to Lot's descendants.
Both verses serve as an identity key linking Esau personally to the nation of Edom in the introduction of the genealogy.
The repetition of this identification at the end of the genealogy confirms that all of Esau's lineage is defined by the name Edom.
This verse directly links Esau's original settlement in Seir to the existing nation of Edom during Moses' time.
The verse explains how Esau's settlement in Seir occurred through God's hand, allowing them to displace the original inhabitants.
This verse theologically anchors Esau's settlement in Seir as a direct gift from God, not merely a random relocation.
This verse highlights the future destiny of the land where Esau settled by prophesying Israel's conquest of Seir.
The verse serves as a concluding confirmation of the identity established in the source verse, framing the chapter about Edom's patriarch.
